description: The figure illustrates five schematic bar-chart shapes used to represent different distribution patterns, shown as separate small panels labeled (from left to right) with an unlabeled first panel, then “Uniform,” “Decreasing,” “Spindle,” and “Bottleneck.” In each panel, the category axis is horizontal with four adjacent bars (no explicit category names or tick marks), and the value axis is vertical with no numeric label, units, tick labels, or visible scale markings. In the unlabeled first panel, four pale green bars increase from left to right, with the first bar shortest, the second slightly taller, the third noticeably taller, and the fourth tallest. In the “Uniform” panel, four pale green bars are equal height. In the “Decreasing” panel, four pale green bars decrease from left to right, with the first tallest and the fourth shortest. In the “Spindle” panel, the first and fourth bars are short while the second and third bars are taller and approximately equal, forming a symmetric middle-high shape. In the “Bottleneck” panel, the first and fourth bars are taller and approximately equal, while the second and third bars are shorter and approximately equal, forming a symmetric middle-low shape. There is no legend, no annotations on individual bars, and no visual emphasis beyond the consistent pale green fill and black outlines; within each panel the bars are arranged left-to-right without an indicated sorting rule beyond the depicted shape.
